description: nunchaku's `pack_micro_scale` warp-lane interleave for svdq `wscales`: a logical [out, in/16] e4m3 grid written as a seven-sub-axis permutation so each mma warp reads its own scales without a shuffle. The reason a reader that takes these bytes verbatim renders noise.
name: nunchaku.micro-scale
provenance: TRANSCRIBED FROM THE CODE THAT READS THESE BYTES: python-gen-worker `src/gen_worker/models/svdq_layout.py` — `_micro_logical(out_f, ng) = (out_f // 128, 1, 4, 4, 8, ng // 4, 4)` (line 111, with `_WARP_N = 128`, `_MICRO_ROW_DIMS = (1, 4, 4, 8)`, `_INSN_K // BLOCK = 64 // 16 = 4`) and `_MICRO_FWD_PERM = (0, 5, 1, 4, 3, 2, 6)` (line 19). This record is those two constants and nothing else.

THE SILENT-ERROR CLASS THIS ENTRY EXISTS FOR, quoted from that module's own docstring: the (4, 4, 8) row split is NOT (4, 8, 4) — the wrong one reshapes without error and silently permutes channels. A permutation written as reviewed code is ratified by somebody noticing; written as data it is ratified by applying it and its inverse and comparing bytes.

EXACT, NOT PADDED: the factors multiply to the logical dims exactly, so out % 128 == 0 and (in/16) % 4 == 0 are enforced by the exact division in the extents themselves. Those are the same two conditions `unpack_wscales` raises SvdqLayoutError on (line 118) — the guard is now the arithmetic rather than a hand-written check beside it.
